text: dsh-annotate 是 DeepSeek Harness 浏览器标注插件，通过 /annotate 命令连接本机 Chrome/Chromium 扩展。用户可选择网页元素并评论，采集选择器、文本、样式和可访问性信息，提交后将整理后的反馈与可选视口截图发送给 agent。适合网页设计评审和前端问题定位；无需 API Key，需连接浏览器扩展。

dsh-annotate lets DeepSeek Harness users select browser elements, add comments, and send DOM, style, accessibility details, and an optional viewport screenshot to an agent through a local Chrome extension.

dsh-annotate「网页元素标注」：启动 /annotate 后悬停高亮网页元素，点击后输入评论，可多选并提交或取消。
dsh-annotate「采集元素上下文」：记录所选元素的选择器、文本、属性、样式、边界和基础可访问性信息。
dsh-annotate「提交标注与截图」：把格式化元素信息发送给 agent，并可附加当前可见视口 PNG。
dsh-annotate「指定目标页面」：/annotate 可携带 URL 导航活动标签并等待加载后开始标注。
dsh-annotate「Select and comment」：Run /annotate to select elements, add comments, then submit or cancel.
dsh-annotate「Capture context」：Collect an element selector, text, styles, bounds, accessibility details, and comment.
dsh-annotate「Send annotations」：Send element details and optionally a visible-tab PNG to the agent.
dsh-annotate「Open target URL」：Pass a URL to /annotate to navigate the active tab before annotation.

dsh-annotate README · dsh-annotate：Visual browser feedback for DeepSeek Harness. `/annotate` asks the companion Chrome extension to enter selection mode; each selected element contributes a selector, DOM facts, computed style highlights, accessibility data, a comment, and an optional viewport screenshot to the agent's next turn.

dsh-annotate README · Why this exists 💡：Browser UI problems are difficult to describe precisely through plain text. `dsh-annotate` lets you point at the relevant element and send the Agent the surrounding browser facts, so visual feedback stays attached to the page element instead of becoming a vague description or a copied screenshot.

dsh-annotate README · Features ✨：- Select elements directly in Chrome or Chromium through `/annotate`.
- Capture selectors, DOM facts, computed-style highlights, accessibility data, comments, and optional viewport screenshots.
- Send structured annotations to the Agent through a local loopback WebSocket bridge.
- Restrict browser connections by loopback host, extension origin, and optional extension ID.

dsh-annotate README · Install 📦：Add the plugin project to a Harness profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile demo add ./dsh-annotate
```

Then install the companion extension:

1. Open `chrome://extensions` in Chrome or Chromium.
2. Enable **Developer mode**.
3. Choose **Load unpacked** and select this project's `browser-extension` directory.
4. Open the extension popup and keep the default bridge endpoint.
dsh-annotate README · Install 📦：For tighter local authorization, copy the extension ID shown in the popup into `allowedExtensionId` in a later Harness patch layer.

dsh-annotate README · Use 🚀：```text
/annotate
/annotate http://localhost:3000
```

Click an element, enter its comment, and repeat as needed. **Submit** sends all captured facts and the visible-tab screenshot to the agent. **Escape** cancels.

dsh-annotate README · Configure ⚙️：```yaml
- id: dsh-annotate
  name: dsh-annotate
  config:
    host: 127.0.0.1

The server refuses non-loopback hosts and browser connections whose origin is not `chrome-extension://`. An empty `allowedExtensionId` accepts any locally installed Chrome extension; set the exact ID for stricter isolation.

dsh-annotate README · Develop 🧑‍💻：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run check
```

Commit the generated `lib/` files with source changes so Git installs include the declared package entry before build scripts run.

Reload the unpacked browser extension after editing its files.

dsh-annotate README · Scope 🎯：Version 0.1 targets one local Chrome/Chromium browser, one active tab, and visible-viewport screenshots. Remote browsers, full-page capture, edit recording, and inline draggable note cards are deferred.

dsh-annotate README · Credits 🙏：The interaction is inspired by [`pi-annotate`](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-annotate). This implementation is built around Harness's human-command, attachment, and Agent APIs and uses a small loopback WebSocket bridge instead of a native-messaging host.
